title: Anthem singer apologizes for botched O Canada lyrics at Leafs game against Islanders
summary: The anthem singer at the Toronto Maple Leafs game against New York Monday night apologized on social media after singing the wrong lyrics to the Canadian national anthem.

image.caption: Former Broadway actress Sarrah Strimel Bentley asked Canadian fans for grace in a tearful Instagram video and said she practiced the Canadian anthem but got nervous in front of the crowd of thousands. (@sarrahstrimelbentley/Instagram)

blocks.text: Toronto
The anthem singer at the Toronto Maple Leafs game against New York Monday night apologized on social media after singing the wrong lyrics to the Canadian national anthem.
Former broadway actress Sarrah Strimel Bentley repeatedly sang ‘we lend out hearts to thee’
The anthem singer at the Toronto Maple Leafs game against New York Monday night apologized on social media after singing the wrong lyrics to O Canada.
Sarrah Strimel Bentley, a former Broadway actress, bungled the words to the Canadian national anthem multiple times during her performance at UBS Arena in New York on Monday.
“We lend our hearts to thee,” the singer sang repeatedly, missing the mark on the correct lyrics, “we stand on guard for thee.”
She also messed up the words in other places, singing, “True patriot love, with all of us command,” rather than, “in all of us command.”

Videos of the anthem circulated online immediately afterwards and social media was flooded with reactions from fans who were unhappy with Bentley's rendition.
“This is disgraceful,” said one user on X.
“Anthem singer on Long Island is just making up her own words,” wrote another.

Many of the social media posts included clips of Leafs fans looking confused in the stands, along with clips of Leafs captain Auston Matthews who appeared perplexed as the wrong lyrics echoed through the arena.
Bentley apologized for the fumble in a tearful video she posted on Instagram during the game.
“I botched the lyrics and I’m really sorry,” she said in the video, adding that she loves Canada.
Bentley said she had repeatedly practiced O Canada, but "getting up in front of 18,000 people and singing an anthem that you haven't heard for your whole life is scary.”
Monday was the New York Islanders’ Hockey Fights Cancer Night. Bentley said breast cancer treatment caused her to enter menopause which can cause lapses in memory.
“I just wish that you’d be a little easier on someone who’s just a human being,” she said, visibly choked up in the video.
Jake McCabe, would lend my heart to thee https://t.co/Qi1U3YWoIm—MapleLeafs
The Maple Leafs beat the Islanders four to two Monday night, ending the team's nine-game losing streak. The club poked fun at the anthem debacle in social media posts.
One of the team’s posts featured a clip of Leafs defenseman Jake McCabe scoring the team’s first goal of the game. “Jake McCabe, would lend my heart to thee,” the post reads.
“Thou lend, thou win,” the team wrote on X following the win.
